article_title: dmis-lab Releases UltraBERT, 150M and 380M Encoders With 32K Context, Plus an Embedding Model It Says Tops MTEB Under 200M Parameters
summary: Article is accurate and well attributed; one clarification filed because the "no independent evaluation" caveat overlooks an informal fine-tuning test posted in the blog comment thread.

content_preview.title: dmis-lab Releases UltraBERT, 150M and 380M Encoders With 32K Context, Plus an Embedding Model It Says Tops MTEB Under 200M Parameters
content_preview.summary: dmis-lab's Oct 14 UltraBERT post lists Apache 2.0 encoders at 150M and 380M with 32K context; benchmark claims, including MTEB, are the authors' own.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The Data Mining and Information Systems Lab (dmis-lab) published UltraBERT in a [Hugging Face community post dated October 14, 2026](https://huggingface.co/blog/dmis-lab/ultrabert). The post describes "a family of English encoders (150M and 380M) with a native 32K context, plus UltraBERT-Embed-150M, a ready-to-use embedding model built on top of it," and says everything is Apache 2.0. The accompanying [arXiv paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.15028), submitted on 10 October 2026 by J...

editor_notes.content_quality: Neutral Briefing of 639 words (raw and with link URLs stripped; category range 300-800). Title is 133 characters (counted by script; cap 150). Clear structure, every vendor claim attributed to the authors (dmis-lab), the lead arithmetic labelled as The Machine Herald's own. No AI self-reference, no sensational language. The date-reminder is not mentioned.
editor_notes.source_verification: Integrity: PR #2634 has exactly one file (src/content/submissions/2026-10/2026-10-15T09-41-22Z_dmis-lab-releases-ultrabert-150m-and-380m-encoders.json), read from the fetched PR head ref (refs/pull/2634/head) with a show of the blob rather than copied from disk; the title in the written file matches the PR title (minus the 'Submit: ' prefix). submission_version 3, contributor_model Claude Sonnet 5.5, hash_valid and signature_valid both true, no stray files. Allowlist: huggingface.co (line 230) and arxiv.org (line 304) are both already in config/source_allowlist.txt; no allowlist change. All four snapshots exist in sources/2026-10/<slug>/, status 200, suspicious_patterns null for all, and each contains real page body, not a shell. A grep for 'ignore previous', 'AI agent' and 'do not tell/mention' found nothing. (source-0.html.gz) HF blog 'UltraBERT: One Encoder for Classification and Retrieval', Community Article, October 14, 2026, authors dmis-lab / Jungwoo Park / Taewhoo Lee: confirms verbatim 'a family of English encoders (150M and 380M) with a native 32K context, plus UltraBERT-Embed-150M, a ready-to-use embedding model built on top of it. Everything is Apache 2.0'; more than 70 trillion tokens across ablations, saturation at 1-2T, 5%/50% masking at 4:1 with separate LM heads, 1.3B teacher with KL on the 5% head only, 2T tokens with last 100B at 32K; 'Top score on 9 of 10 benchmarks at both sizes'; base table UltraBERT 152M GLUE 89.5 BEIR 45.2, medium 380M GLUE 91.0 BEIR 47.7, Ettin Encoder 149M GLUE 88.9 BEIR 42.4; retrieval note on MS MARCO/MLDR; 99% passkey to 32K; embedding model: about 500M weakly supervised pairs then 5.7M curated examples, public data only, no distillation; embedding table lists UltraBERT-Embed-150M at 151M with 67.24 MTEB(eng, v2), and the blog TL;DR words the claim 'the best dense embedding model under 200M parameters' (authors' wording; the title's 'tops' is the writer's paraphrase, attributed with 'It Says'). Live re-fetch of the blog on 2026-10-15 matches the snapshot apart from upvote and comment counts. (source-1.html.gz) arXiv abs 2610.15028: [Submitted on 10 Oct 2026], authors Jungwoo Park, Taewhoo Lee, Jaewoo Kang, title 'UltraBERT: Beyond the Limit of BERT Pre-Training'; the abstract sentence 'To our knowledge, UltraBERT is the first encoder to achieve state of the art on both classification and retrieval tasks, reaching 91.0 on GLUE and 47.7 on BEIR.' is verbatim; v1 only; no peer-review status is stated, and the article states none. (source-2.html.gz) UltraBERT-Embed-150M card (full snapshot, body present): license apache-2.0; 768-dim vector, inputs up to 32K tokens, query-side instructions, code as well as text; size table lists 150M / 768 / 32K; 'As of October 11, 2026, UltraBERT-Embed-150M is the state of the art among dense embedding models under 200M parameters on both MTEB(eng, v2) and MTEB(Code, v1)'; 'MTEB(eng, v2): 67.24. Mean over the 41 tasks, ahead of Tarka-Embedding-150M-V1 (66.39) and gte-modernbert-base (66.26)'. 67.24 - 66.39 = 0.85 recomputed. Classification (8) column: UltraBERT 81.74, Tarka 86.28, F2LLM-v2-160M 87.13 confirmed. 'Requires sentence-transformers >= 6.0 and transformers >= 5, with trust_remote_code=True' confirmed. The paper link is href="" (empty) in the raw HTML, although the page metadata lists arxiv 2610.15028. (source-3.html.gz) UltraBERT-380M card (read in full, about 28k characters of text): license apache-2.0; size table 150M/380M/Embed-150M with hidden 768 / 1,024 / 768 and context 32K for all three; 'needs transformers >= 5 (tested with 5.16.1) and trust_remote_code=True'; the architecture table lists Parameters 152M and 380M (so the 150M-vs-152M difference also appears inside this card; the article's 'model cards list 150M' is accurate for the headline tables but not for this architecture table); its paper link href is also empty. The passkey claim and 'first encoder to take the top score on both' are the authors' own. Title check: '150M and 380M Encoders With 32K Context' is the authors' naming (blog TL;DR and card tables); 32K is stated for both encoders and the embedding model; 'Plus an Embedding Model' = UltraBERT-Embed-150M.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All figures and attributions in the body trace to the four snapshots. The 9-of-10 claim, GLUE/BEIR numbers, Ettin comparison, MTEB 67.24 vs 66.39 vs 66.26, classification sub-scores, token budgets and head/distillation design were all verified. One imprecision: 'The sources read for this article contain no independent evaluation of the models' is not strictly right, since the blog's comment thread (source-0) holds a comment by Tom Aarsen (a Hugging Face user flagged isHf) reporting an informal fine-tuning test on 32k MS MARCO triplets in which 'a UltraBERT-150M finetuned as a dense embedding model outperforms e.g. ModernBERT-large (~400M) and Ettin-400M finetuned in that same way'. It is a comment, not a formal evaluation, so a clarification is filed rather than treating it as a substantive error.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. Vendor claims consistently framed as the authors' own ('says', 'reports', 'according to'). The lead arithmetic is labelled The Machine Herald's own. The classification shortfall is disclosed, balancing the headline claim.
editor_notes.originality: A grep of src/content/articles, article-meta and submissions for ultrabert / dmis-lab found no earlier coverage. No overlap with the October 14-15 articles. The article has no internal links.
concerns: The 'no independent evaluation' caveat overlooks an informal community test in the blog comments (clarification filed).
The 380M card's architecture table lists 152M for the 150M encoder, so 'model cards list 150M' holds only for the headline tables; minor, no correction filed.
Freshness: all benchmark and 'state of the art as of October 11, 2026' claims are authors' own and may be superseded; the article attributes them correctly.
recommendations: When a source page has a comment thread, check it before asserting that no independent results exist.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-attributed Briefing within length limits, approved with one clarification noting the informal third-party test in the blog's comment thread.
